requirements.action: User clicks the row titled exactly `Add project`.
requirements.expected_result: A modal folder chooser opens with the confirm-button text exactly `Add project` and the message exactly `Choose a folder for your agents to work in.` (note the full stop). Files cannot be chosen; multiple folders can. On confirm, each chosen folder becomes a project named after its last path component, with its project scripts loaded from the folder; a folder already present by standardised path yields the existing project rather than a duplicate. A new thread is then created in the last project of the iteration. On cancel nothing at all happens.
side_effects: Opens a modal system file dialog.
Reads the chosen folder for a project scripts file (ProjectFile.scripts).
Schedules a library save.
Creates a thread, which writes the library.

failure_cases: Dialog cancelled (`runModal() != .OK`): no project, no thread, no save.
A folder already added: `addProject(at:)` returns the existing project; no duplicate row appears, and if it is the last url, a new thread is still created in that existing project.
requirements.cancellation: Cancelling the dialog aborts everything; the loop has not started.
requirements.windows_path: Windows uses IFileOpenDialog with FOS_PICKFOLDERS and FOS_ALLOWMULTISELECT. The confirm button text is set to `Add project` (SetOkButtonLabel) and the message to `Choose a folder for your agents to work in.` (SetFileNameLabel/SetTitle as the Windows dialog allows). Path standardisation must be the Windows canonical form, and the duplicate check must be case-insensitive on Windows paths where macOS compared a standardised POSIX path; this is a platform boundary and the comparison rule is recorded in port_impacts.
requirements.verification_method: interaction test with a stubbed chooser returning one, several and zero folders; contract fixture for the duplicate-path rule.

requirements.preconditions: A row is grabbed and a pointer move has been delivered.
requirements.action: The visual offset exceeds half the sum of the grabbed row's slot and the next neighbour's slot, in either direction.
requirements.expected_result: The neighbour and the grabbed row swap. The test is a strict greater-than against `(own + slot) / 2 + slot * pastCentre`, with pastCentre zero in the sidebar, so the swap fires the moment the centre is crossed. The loop repeats, so one fast flick can cross several rows in a single delivery. If the move closure returns false the loop breaks without advancing the index and without adding the compensation. Each accepted swap adds or subtracts the neighbour's slot height from `settled`, which keeps the row pinned under the pointer while the list flows around it. The compensation must be applied inside `settle`, not inside the move closure, because `settle` mutates a copy of the caller's state.

requirements.windows_path: Direct translation of the arithmetic. A void-returning move callback would reorder forever past a refused move (port_impacts 154), so the Bool return is mandatory. The fallback height is the literal 29 (Chrome.rowHeight 28 plus the list's 1 pt spacing).

requirements.title: Deleting a thread removes its children, selects a neighbour, reports a running head as interrupted, discards its state, deletes its checkpoints and optionally its worktree
source_evidence: DroppyCode/App/AppModel.swift:934-959 delete(_:removeWorktree:) - `guard let thread = thread(id) else { return }`; `for helper in children(of: id) { delete(helper.id) }`; `if selectedThreadID == id { selectNeighbor(of: id) }`; `if thread.isHydraHead, thread.hydra?.isFinished == false { finishHydraHead(id, status: .interrupted, summary: nil) }`; `discardThreadState(thread)`; `threads.removeAll { $0.id == id }`; then, with the project, `let worktree = removeWorktree || thread.hydra?.hasOwnCopy == true ? thread.worktreePath : nil` and `Task { await git.deleteCheckpoints(thread: id); if let worktree { try? await git.removeWorktree(at: worktree) } }`; `updateDockBadge()`; `saveLibrary()`
requirements.expected_result: Every child is deleted first, recursively, including panelled ones. If the thread was selected a neighbour is selected. A Hydra head deleted mid-job reports to its lead as interrupted so the batch settles. The thread's state and history are discarded and it is removed from the library. Its Git checkpoints are deleted asynchronously. Its worktree is removed only when the user chose `Delete thread and worktree`, or when the thread is a head whose working copy the app itself made. The dock badge is refreshed and the library is written immediately. Worktree removal failures are swallowed (`try?`).
side_effects: Deletes the thread's stored document.
Runs Git checkpoint deletion and, conditionally, worktree removal in the background.
Updates the dock badge.
Writes the library.
requirements.persistence: The thread is removed from Library.threads; the library is saved immediately.
failure_cases: Thread missing: nothing happens.
Git worktree removal fails: the error is discarded and the thread is still gone.
Project missing: no Git work at all is scheduled, so checkpoints are left behind.
requirements.cancellation: not cancellable once started; the Git work is fire-and-forget.
requirements.windows_path: Git worktree removal on Windows must cope with locked files and long paths; failures are still swallowed to preserve parity. Platform boundary: file system and Git.
requirements.verification_method: contract fixture asserting the recursion, the head interruption and the two worktree conditions.

requirements.preconditions: A context menu is opened on a row.
requirements.action: User chooses Rename, Delete, Settle or Reopen.
requirements.expected_result: The menu's closure writes a value into a box the list owns (rename, delete) or into the model (finish request) and returns. No menu closure holds a strong reference to the row's state storage, its frames or its settle handlers, and every one holds the model weakly and bails when it is gone. requirements.action: User chooses `Remove project` from the project's ellipsis popover or its context menu.
requirements.expected_result: Owner ruling OD-0008 A9 (a named deviation): while `settings.confirmBeforeDeleting` is true (the default), choosing `Remove project` removes nothing yet; it asks for confirmation first, as thread deletion does, and only a confirmed request runs the removal. While it is false the removal runs at once, as upstream. The removal itself is upstream's: every thread of that project has its state discarded and is removed from the library, then the project itself is removed. If the project was the remembered last project that memory is cleared. If the selection no longer resolves to a thread the selection is cleared. The library is saved on the debounce, not immediately. There is no undo and no worktree or checkpoint cleanup: unlike `delete(_:)` this path does not touch Git at all, so a removed project's threads leave their checkpoints and worktrees on disk.
